clue.text: Making a tidy sum?

parts.note: reads as doing a neat bit of arithmetic, but means earning a large profit, or literally tidying a room

explanation.surface: Someone working a neat calculation.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is both making a big profit and putting things in order, so 'tidy sum' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to make a fortune quickly, a tidy sum being a lot of money.

clue.text: Firm using a litre of fuel

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company getting through a litre of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a solid fossil fuel burnt for heat and power.

clue.text: Talk at length of Briton abroad one took in

parts.note: an expat is someone, such as a Briton, living outside their home country
I is the Roman numeral for one
took in, as food, means ate

explanation.surface: Gossip about a Briton overseas who welcomed a lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write in great detail on a subject.

clue.text: Wants to talk when one makes bread

indicators.note: said when spoken, so the following word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a baker kneads the dough when making bread

explanation.surface: Someone who longs to chat while baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs as a verb is a synonym for wants or requires.

clue.text: Values put on anaesthetics

explanation.surface: Prices added for painkillers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as 'numb-ers', things that numb; 'put on' just links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Values are figures or quantities, and humorously anaesthetics are things that deaden feeling.

clue.text: A tool that may suit Len

indicators.note: suggests the words suit and Len may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A gadget that would be just right for someone called Len.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' is the anagram signal: SUIT LEN reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a household implement, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Author of "Dorian" will, it's said, have an ego

explanation.surface: A novelist's legacy, so people say, is pure vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Self wrote the novel 'Dorian, an Imitation'; 'will' is his first name, not a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Self is the novelist behind Dorian; and the ego is one's own personal identity.

clue.text: A predatory bird some Tuareg retreat from

indicators.note: only part of the words Tuareg retreat is taken, showing a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A hunting bird that drives some desert nomads back.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a heron that preys on fish and frogs.

clue.text: In which one finds roots?

parts.note: suggests plant roots in the soil, but means ancestry traced on a chart

explanation.surface: Asking where to look for a plant's roots.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogical chart of ancestors and descendants shows a person's origins.

clue.text: First sample is missing, but there's plenty left

indicators.note: points at the opening letter of the word sample as the one to go
says that letter is absent from what remains of the word

explanation.surface: One specimen has gone, but there are many more.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than enough, an abundant supply.

clue.text: Malts more thoroughly mixed in whirlpool

indicators.note: tells us the letters of malts more are well stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Whisky stirred hard in a swirling vortex.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirling current of water.

clue.text: Wandered off street, ready for diversion

indicators.note: a diversion sends the letters of ready on a different route into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone left the road, prepared for a detour.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to roam away from the proper path.

clue.text: Such people are always trying!

parts.note: sounds like a complaint about tiresome folk, but means people who constantly try things out

explanation.surface: A grumble about irritating people.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who test things are forever making trials of them.

clue.text: Rodent the Spanish also called a glutton

parts.note: a rat is a common rodent
el is the Spanish masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A rodent that is also known as a greedy eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rodent' looks like the definition but gives only RAT; the ratel, or honey badger, was also called a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, an omnivorous animal also named the glutton in old natural histories.

clue.text: Possibly aggrieve by taking ship which is hostile

indicators.note: the rearranged word swallows another piece in its middle
signals that aggrieve might be rearranged into another order

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Upsetting someone by commandeering a vessel is an unfriendly act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' shuffles AGGRIEVE into AGGREIVE; 'by taking' puts SS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive behaviour is belligerent and confrontational.

clue.text: Dolphin's a lightweight, gets half-pushed aside

parts.note: a gram is a tiny unit of weight

indicators.note: only the first half of the word pushed is kept

explanation.surface: A small dolphin is shoved out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-' takes the first three letters of PUSHED; 'gets' and 'aside' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The grampus is Risso's dolphin, a stout cetacean of temperate seas.

clue.text: Baseball player acquires vessel

explanation.surface: A ballplayer gets hold of a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: The pitcher throws the ball in baseball; a pitcher is also a large jug.

clue.text: Knocks flat and prepares for burial

explanation.surface: Someone floors a man and readies the body for the funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out is to fell someone with a blow, and also to dress a corpse for burial.

clue.text: Primate's name rang out, getting an unruly answer

indicators.note: an unruly crowd is disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: The ape's name was called, and the reply was rowdy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting an' only joins the pieces; N, RANG OUT and A are all shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Landlord needs a key to get back in

indicators.note: here means takes inside itself, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a landlord rents property out, a renter
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: The landlord requires a key to let himself back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' works as a container signal: RENTER takes E after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into a place is to enter it again.

clue.text: His pictures always give a rosy view

definitions.text: His pictures always give a rosy view

parts.words: His pictures always give a rosy view
parts.note: sounds like an optimistic painter, but refers literally to an artist famous for painting roses

explanation.surface: An artist whose work is always cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre-Joseph Redouté was a Belgian-French botanical artist celebrated for his watercolours of roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Redouté's best-known work, Les Roses, shows flowers in exquisite detail.

clue.text: A trade in which I could shine

indicators.note: suggests the words a trade and I could be made into something else by reordering

explanation.surface: A line of work in which one might excel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' is only a link; A TRADE plus I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to give out light or glow.

clue.text: Footballers who get around?

parts.note: ... is a Glasgow football club, and ... are also people who roam widely

explanation.surface: Asking which players travel a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a famous Scottish football club in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the Glasgow club share their name with wanderers and park wardens.

clue.text: Cut second hair

parts.note: a lash is an eyelash, a single hair

explanation.surface: A trim of the hair, done a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A slash is a long cut made with a sweeping stroke.

clue.text: Room assigned to an Athenian

explanation.surface: A chamber allocated to a man from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a loft space under the roof; Attic also means belonging to ancient Athens.

clue.text: Moving quickly may gain cnd manoeuvrability

indicators.note: the ability to move around freely, so the letters of gain and cnd are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Swift movement may help a nuclear disarmament campaign get room to act.
explanation.walkthrough: CND is Britain's Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament; 'may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing is lively rhythmic movement, as of flickering light or skipping feet.

clue.text: A short preface

parts.note: an opening section, and also a word that is itself a clipped form

explanation.definitionFit: This clipped form of introduction is a brief opening passage of music or text.

clue.text: Sadly, no time for geography book

indicators.note: says the following piece is absent, so it is taken out of the book

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.surface: Unfortunately there is no time for the map book.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection expresses grief or regret, like unfortunately.

clue.text: It may be enjoyable but it's not playtime!

definitions.text: It may be enjoyable but it's not playtime!

parts.words: It may be enjoyable but it's not playtime!
parts.note: suggests a school break, but means the pause between acts when the play is not running

explanation.surface: A teacher telling children that fun is not the same as a break.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval in a theatre is the time when no play is being performed.

clue.text: Taking a drink with a student, that's all

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Having a quick nip with an undergraduate, and that's everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The total is the whole amount, everything added together.

clue.text: Behold, how the common market is two-faced!

parts.note: EC is the European Community, once called the Common Market

indicators.note: a face looking both ways, so the same letters appear also turned back

parts.note: EC is the European Community, once called the Common Market

explanation.surface: Look at how duplicitous the European trading bloc is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is two-faced' means EC shown one way and then backwards; 'how the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecce is Latin for look or see, as in Ecce Homo.

clue.text: Reporters for "the field"?

parts.note: the field is the body of riders in a hunt, so its hounds might bring it news

explanation.surface: Asking who writes for a country-sports magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Field is a British country-sports magazine; in fox hunting, the field is the followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists eager for a story are nicknamed after hunting dogs on the scent.
